participants: Andrew Musial (closer; recorded under the Fathom speaker label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)')
summary: Mid-week team meeting. Opens with two operational faults — a prospect (Nikhil Amin) who showed up for a call that the closer's calendar had booked for Saturday while the setter had booked it for that day, and a call from Andrew Jin, a former coach, appearing inside the Fathom account the current closer uses. The bulk of the meeting is a coaching block on financial qualification of leads, in which the manager and closer set out when a setter should pre-frame price, using country of residence, occupation and third-party credit data (income, available credit, credit score) as the screens. A live example is worked through: a US chauffeur with a stated $3,000 budget, $70,000 income, $6,000 available credit and a 654 credit score, with the manager coaching Kim to set him anyway and Andrew to assemble payment from card plus Klarna financing. After Kim leaves it becomes a 1-1: reviewing a retired police officer who walked off a call at the price reveal, a prospect with unresolved gut symptoms awaiting blood tests, and a long conversation about conviction, ego and bodybuilding.
notable: Price architecture stated by the manager is wider than the audited offer: 'he could do one year of Primal U for 2K, or if he wants to spend an extra $1,000 and wants more customized coaching than he could do the three months' — implying a three-month option at roughly $3,000, while the closer had quoted $4,000 for three months on two sales calls the same day.

Financial qualification is explicitly geographic and occupational: Europeans, Mexicans, South Americans and 'a doctor in India' are named as needing a price pre-frame; baristas, Starbucks and Chick-fil-A staff and teachers are named as red flags; US leads earning '60 to 70k a year' are green-flagged.

The closer generalised about UK prospects — 'there's this, no offense, U.K. mentality that they don't invest in themselves' — and the manager pushed back immediately: 'I would be very careful running that thought process.'

Third-party consumer financial data on prospects is used at set time: 'you're going to be able to look at the sales kick financial data and see what it graded them.' Kim read out a named prospect's income, available credit and credit score on the call.

Manager coached splitting a purchase across card and consumer credit: 'if there's a certain amount that they want to pay on card do that first get them to pay it and then do the other amount in the custom payment thing and then try to have them check out with Klarna to finance the rest.' Klarna acceptance is described as poor: 'we just haven't had a lot of people accepted with it.'

Setters are instructed not to give the price when asked: 'they're asking how much is it? Of course, we... We don't say how much is it, but giving them, like, a ballpark.' Kim reported telling a prospect the price 'was custom'.
The closer reported a deal closed the previous day to a client with 'some back, serious back issues' with no mention of medical clearance.

The manager gave the correct instruction on a health-gated prospect: 'If somebody says they have clear health things that they need to figure out before they were to commit to a program, then they should figure out their health things first to even see what sort of a program could make sense for them.' The closer had described having 'sort of diagnosed' the same prospect's gut symptoms on the call.

Setter-call recordings are not reliably captured — some setter calls happen on Zoom or WhatsApp, and the manager notes 'the only other reason there wouldn't be a recording is if Kim forgot to hit his Fathom'.

The Fathom speaker label 'Andrew Jin (Primal Instinct)' that appears on every transcript in this folder belongs to a former coach, not to the current closer: 'there's a call from Andrew Jin, the former coach' and 'it's weird that he's still somehow able to get in to a Fathom that isn't his.'

Setter targeting is deliberately loosened when the calendar is light: 'when calendars were a little bit lighter, you started less financially qualifying to get more momentum back on the calendar because that's what you have to do.' This makes lead quality a function of calendar fill, which will confound any close-rate comparison across weeks.
